solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Hands on top beginning to slacken bolt (3,5)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, A on B puts A after B, so the hands come after the top
indicatorNotes.beginning to: takes only the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle
first letter of slacken
hands = crew, as in 'all hands on deck'

annotation.surface: A mechanic's tip: keep your hands on top while starting to loosen a bolt.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as instructions for loosening a bolt, but 'bolt' is the definition and 'Hands' is a noun for sailors.
annotation.definitionFit: A cap screw is a kind of bolt with a cylindrical head.

entries.clue: Moving melody captures minstrel’s heart (5)

indicatorNotes.captures: the melody holds the other letters inside it

blocks.note: an air is a tune
the middle two letters of the eight-letter minstrel

annotation.surface: A touching song seems to win over the soul of a travelling singer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Moving' looks like it means touching, describing the melody; it is the definition, meaning up and about.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone up and about after rising is moving, not moved emotionally.

entries.clue: Where kippers may be found in Britain backed opening fish stores (8,3)

indicatorNotes.backed: sends the opening and the fish backwards
indicatorNotes.stores: the reversed letters hold IN GB inside them

blocks.note: eels are fish; reversed they give SLEE
a gap is an opening; reversed it gives PAG
IN plus GB, the abbreviation for Great Britain, stored inside the reversed letters

annotation.surface: An odd note on where to find smoked herring, involving British fish shops.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about kippers the smoked fish, and 'fish' nearby helps the trap; here a kipper is someone having a kip, British slang for a sleep. 'Backed' turns both the opening and the fish round together, as one string.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone kipping, or sleeping, may well be found in a sleeping bag.

entries.clue: Craft capsized, engulfed by sticky substance in hold (8)

indicatorNotes.capsized: a capsized boat is upside down, so in a down clue the word is written backwards
indicatorNotes.engulfed by: the reversed word goes inside the sticky substance

blocks.note: resin is the sticky stuff from trees; it wraps round the craft
craft = art, skill; capsized it reads TRA

annotation.surface: A boat has overturned and is stuck in something gluey below decks.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Craft' a boat, which fits 'capsized' and 'hold'; it means skill, and 'hold' is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to hold a struggling person is to keep them in check.

entries.clue: With advanced gunship drifting on water, possibly it’s next to sink? (7-2,6)

indicatorNotes.drifting: the letters of gunship move about into a new order
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, A on B puts A after B, so the water goes last

blocks.note: w is the standard abbreviation for with
A for advanced, as in A level
the letters of gunship rearranged
water is one example of a liquid

annotation.surface: A warship drifting at sea raises the worry that it's the next to go down.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface says 'sink' as in go down, keeping up the sea picture; the definition means the kitchen sink. Washing-up is British for washing the dishes, so this is dish soap.
annotation.definitionFit: Washing-up liquid is dish soap, and the bottle usually stands next to the kitchen sink.

entries.clue: Suspicious about new drink (6)

blocks.note: shady = suspicious, dodgy
n is the abbreviation for new

annotation.surface: Someone is wary of a new drink.
annotation.walkthrough: A shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, a common British pub drink.
annotation.definitionFit: A British pub drink of beer mixed with lemonade, so the bare word 'drink' covers it.

entries.clue: For example, pump protecting very large excavator (6)

indicatorNotes.protecting: the shoe wraps round the V

blocks.note: a pump is a kind of shoe, a light slip-on; it wraps round the V
v is the abbreviation for very
l is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

annotation.surface: A pump shielding a huge digging machine, perhaps on a building site.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pump' looks like a machine for water on the site; in Britain it is also a light shoe, like a plimsoll.
annotation.definitionFit: A shovel digs, so it is an excavator, just a small hand-held one.

entries.clue: Fitting old train with tilting system (3)

blocks.note: the adjective: suitable, right for the occasion
the Advanced Passenger Train, a British Rail train of the 1980s that tilted on bends, known by its initials

annotation.surface: Kitting out an old train with a system that lets it lean on curves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fitting' reads as a verb, installing the system; it is the adjective. The APT was an experimental British train of the 1980s that tilted into corners.
annotation.definitionFit: Apt means fitting or appropriate, and APT was the name of the tilting train.

entries.clue: Faint sound turned up to check note for amplitude (9)

indicatorNotes.turned up: in a down clue, turning up means reading from the bottom, so the word goes backwards
indicatorNotes.to check: the reversed sound holds back the note by surrounding it

blocks.note: dim = faint, of light
noise = sound; turned up it reads ESION, which then goes round the N
n is the abbreviation for note

annotation.surface: A quiet sound is turned up so someone can check a note's amplitude, like a sound engineer.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is audio, where 'amplitude' means loudness and 'turned up' means louder; amplitude here means size, or extent.
annotation.definitionFit: Amplitude in its general sense is extent or size, which is a dimension.

entries.clue: Date naked females in capital (6)

indicatorNotes.naked: stripped of its outer layer: the first and last letters come off

blocks.note: DATE without its first and last letters
hens are female birds, and a hen party is all women

annotation.surface: An eyebrow-raising plan to meet undressed women in the city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Naked' sounds like part of the picture; it tells you to strip DATE of its outside letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Greek capital.

entries.clue: Who’s prepared stage for the moment the curtain goes up? (8)

annotation.definition: the moment the curtain goes up

indicatorNotes.prepared: made ready, so the letters of who's are worked into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of who's rearranged
a stage is a period of time

annotation.surface: A theatre manager checks who is ready backstage before the curtain rises.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stage' seems to be the theatre boards; it means a period, as in a stage of life.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the start of a performance is when the curtain rises.

entries.clue: Firm pressure stifles resistance group (4)

indicatorNotes.stifles: firm pressure smothers the R by closing round it

blocks.note: co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
r is the physics symbol for resistance
p is the physics symbol for pressure

annotation.surface: A company's heavy hand is silencing a group of resistance fighters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Resistance group' reads as a band of rebels; the definition is 'group' alone, in the sense of a batch.
annotation.definitionFit: A crop can mean a group or batch, as in this year's crop of graduates.

entries.clue: Fake gem I sent flying into river (10)

indicatorNotes.flying: sends the letters of I sent all over the place
indicatorNotes.into: the rearranged letters go inside the river

blocks.note: the Rhone is a river in France and Switzerland; the rearranged letters go after RH
the letters of I sent rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone confesses to hurling a fake jewel into a river.
annotation.walkthrough: The Rhine is inside the answer, which makes it the obvious river; it is a red herring, since the wordplay needs the RHONE.
annotation.definitionFit: A rhinestone is an imitation diamond made of glass or paste.

entries.clue: In field one leads dog, primarily bone idle, on run (11)

indicatorNotes.primarily: takes only the first letter of bone
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, A on B puts A above B, so idle comes before run

blocks.note: to dog someone is to follow or trail them
first letter of bone
to laze is to idle
r is the cricket abbreviation for run

annotation.surface: A scene in a field: someone walks a lazy dog that is running about.
annotation.walkthrough: The field seems to be grass with a dog on it; it is a field of study or work, where the trailblazer leads the way.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the pioneer who goes first and shows others the way in a field of work.

entries.clue: Screening method for preserving food has succeeded before (8)

indicatorNotes.before: the S stands in front of the canning

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in lists of monarchs
canning is a way of preserving food

annotation.surface: A food-preserving method has already been tried and worked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Screening' could mean a film showing; here it is medical or security checking.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: airport and hospital checks pass people through machines that image them.

entries.clue: Friendly criminal leaving court through middle of gallery (9)

indicatorNotes.leaving: the CT for court comes off the criminal

blocks.note: CONVICT without CT, the abbreviation for court
via = through, by way of
the fourth of gallery's seven letters

annotation.surface: A well-mannered criminal walks out of court by way of the public gallery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' wants to be an adjective; it is the noun, a convict.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: warm and sociable company, the kind found at a good party.

entries.clue: Entering key, one disembarked (4)

indicatorNotes.Entering: to enter something is to go inside it, so the one goes into the letters of the key

blocks.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard; the I goes inside it
I is the Roman numeral for one

annotation.surface: Someone types a key and gets off a vehicle, an odd pairing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key' could be a musical key or an island; it is the Alt key.
annotation.definitionFit: To alight is to get off a train or boat, and alit is its past tense.

entries.clue: Having overturned, swerves around difficult racetrack (8)

indicatorNotes.Having overturned: in a down clue, turning over flips the word end to end
indicatorNotes.around: swerves goes round difficult before the flip

blocks.note: a ship or plane yaws when it swerves off course; DEEP goes in after YAW
deep = hard to understand

annotation.surface: A car that has flipped over swerves round a tricky bend on the track.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a crash on a racecourse, so the definition sits inside the picture. YAW DEEP S is written, then the whole thing flips.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, most often for a dirt oval used for motorcycle racing.

entries.clue: Discards rotating door part (4)

indicatorNotes.rotating: turned right round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to bin something is to throw it away, so discards = bins

annotation.surface: Someone throws out part of a revolving door.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rotating door' suggests a revolving door; 'rotating' reverses BINS, and the definition is 'door part' alone. A snib is a Scottish word for a small door catch.
annotation.definitionFit: A snib is a small bolt or catch on a door or window.

entries.clue: Whistle part of song for distributor? (8)

blocks.note: a pipe is a whistle, a simple wind instrument
a line is part of a song

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether a whistled bit of a tune could go to a music distributor.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as a stretch: a pipeline distributes oil or gas.
annotation.definitionFit: A pipeline carries oil or gas from source to users, distributing it.

entries.clue: Top judge finally back in Ireland (6)

indicatorNotes.finally: takes the last letter of back

blocks.note: j is the abbreviation for judge
Erin is the poetic name for Ireland; the K goes inside it
last letter of back

annotation.surface: The chief judge is at last returning to Ireland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top judge' reads as a senior judge; 'Top' is the definition, a garment.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a sleeveless jacket is a garment worn on the top half.

entries.clue: Two records, one after the other (6,4)

blocks.note: tells you the word records supplies two separate pieces
a single is a record with one song
a file is a record kept on someone

annotation.surface: Two records are played back to back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Two records' gives two different kinds of record: a music single and a paper file.
annotation.definitionFit: Walking in single file means going one after the other.

entries.clue: All for day off — unrestricted, do nothing (4)

indicatorNotes.unrestricted: each word loses its outer letters, the limits that hold it in

blocks.note: the middles of aLl, fOr, dAy and oFf

annotation.surface: A slogan for a day off with no rules: just do nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unrestricted' seems to describe the day off; it strips the outside letters of each of the four words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to idle about or lounge.

entries.clue: Area with gold reserves through which vital fluid is pumped? (5)

annotation.definition: through which vital fluid is pumped?

blocks.note: a is the abbreviation for area
or is gold in heraldry
the TA, or Territorial Army, was Britain's army reserve

annotation.surface: A region holding gold reserves, pumped through like a lifeblood.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like economics, with money as the lifeblood; the fluid is blood and the TA is the British army reserve.
annotation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery, through which the heart pumps blood.

entries.clue: I’m on time but running around UK city (8)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, A on B puts A after B, so I'M follows the T
indicatorNotes.running: the letters of but run into a new order
indicatorNotes.around: the rearranged letters go round UK

blocks.note: t is the abbreviation for time
taken as written
the letters of but rearranged; UK goes after the B
taken as written

annotation.surface: Someone is on schedule but rushing around a British city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'UK city' reads as the definition, but UK is part of the letters and the city is in Mali.
annotation.definitionFit: Timbuktu is a city in Mali, famous as a byword for somewhere remote.

entries.clue: Tree trunk (3)

blocks.note: an evergreen shrub or small tree, often clipped into hedges
here a large chest for storage, not part of a tree

annotation.walkthrough: 'Tree trunk' reads as one thing; it is two separate definitions, with trunk meaning a chest.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are plain: the evergreen used for hedging, and a container, of which a trunk is a large kind.

entries.clue: Excellent design carrying variable current in switch (6)

indicatorNotes.carrying: design holds the two letters inside it
indicatorNotes.in switch: switched round, so the whole thing is read backwards

blocks.note: to draw is to design; ZI goes in before its W
z is a letter used for a variable in algebra
i is the physics symbol for electric current

annotation.surface: An excellent electrical design running a variable current through a switch.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is circuitry, where switch is a component; 'in switch' tells you to switch the letters end to end. Wizard is British slang for excellent.
annotation.definitionFit: Wizard is old-fashioned British slang for excellent.

entries.clue: Warning device in floor interrupted by loose connection at the back (6)

indicatorNotes.interrupted by: the loose letters break into floor
indicatorNotes.at the back: takes the last letter of connection

blocks.note: to floor a boxer is a KO, a knockout
lax = loose, slack; it goes between the K and O
last letter of connection

annotation.surface: An alarm set in the floor keeps getting cut off by a loose wire at the back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Floor' looks like the ground; it is the verb, to knock down.
annotation.definitionFit: A klaxon is a loud electric horn used as a warning.

entries.clue: Fancy old man going round yard on a moped, mostly coming off (8)

indicatorNotes.mostly coming off: most of moped comes away, leaving only its first letter

blocks.note: old man = father, dad
y is the abbreviation for yard; it goes inside DAD
re = on, about, as in memo headers
taken as written
MOPED with most of it, OPED, taken off

annotation.surface: An old man riding round a yard on a scooter keeps falling off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' reads as an adjective; it is the noun, a flight of fancy.
annotation.definitionFit: A fancy is an imagined notion, which is what a daydream is.
